_strings.@@17c75d61fe39: Wisconsin Earned Income Credit (EITC) — Full-year Wisconsin resident who qualifies for the federal earned income credit AND has at least one qualifying child (federal definition of qualifying child applies). Married filers generally must file jointly; a married-filing-separate filer is ineligible unless they meet sec. 7703(b) IRC (then files as head of household, married). Wisconsin adopted the federal EITC changes in Public Law 117-2, but a qualifying child is still required for the Wisconsin credit (no childless-worker credit).

_strings.@@2cec9b3c3709: Wisconsin Department of Revenue, PO Box 59, Madison WI 53785-0001 (if refund or no tax due). Note: if claiming homestead credit, mail to PO Box 34, Madison WI 53786-0001.
_strings.@@332f105251c7: Wisconsin Homestead Credit (property-tax / rent circuit-breaker) — Legal resident of Wisconsin for all of 2023; age 18 or older as of Dec 31, 2023 (claimant); owner or renter of the Wisconsin homestead lived in during 2023; AND must meet one of: age 62+ (claimant), disabled, or have earned income during 2023. Disqualified if: claimed as a dependent on another's 2023 federal return (unless age 62+), living in a tax-exempt nursing home receiving Title XIX medical assistance, received W2/county relief payments for every month of the year, lived all year in property-tax-exempt housing, or another household member filed a Schedule H/H-EZ. Claimed on Schedule H (or simpler Schedule H-EZ).
_strings.@@43752cc4755a: Treaty conformity — WI conforms to federal treaty treatment — income exempt from federal tax under a treaty is also excluded from WI income (it flows through the federal starting point; do not add it back on the WI return). (This is about TREATY conformity only — a state can conform on treaties while DECOUPLING from the federal Code for deductions or credits; see any law-change lines below.) State note: Wisconsin Form 1 starts from federal adjusted gross income (Form 1, Line 1 instructions: "Fill in your federal adjusted gross income from line 11 of your federal Form 1040 or 1040-SR"). Federally treaty-exempt income is already excluded from federal AGI and is never added back on the Wisconsin return. The Schedule AD (Additions to Income) instructions list all addition modifications (lines 1-31: state/municipal interest, capital gain/loss, college savings & ABLE distributions, federal NOL deduction, lump-sum distributions, PFIC excess distributions, related-entity expenses, moving expenses outside WI/US, basis differences, marital property differences, farmland preservation credit, various computed credits, and tax-option (S) corporation adjustments) and NONE adds back income exempt under a U.S. tax treaty. Form 1 Line 2 (adjustments via Schedule I) only converts for federal law provisions Wisconsin has not adopted (e.g., bonus depreciation, business interest limitation), not treaties. Therefore treaty-exempt income flows through and is NOT re-taxed -> conforms = true. (Verified at WI DOR; no explicit treaty provision text found, so flagged in unverified.)

_strings.@@a3c8c336e6d8: Married Couple Credit — Married filing a joint return where both spouses have qualified earned income (taxable wages, salaries, tips, certain scholarships/fellowships reported on W-2, other employee compensation, disability income treated as wages, and net self-employment earnings). Not available if Form 2555/2555-EZ (foreign earned income exclusion) or Form 4563 is filed. Computed on Schedule 2 of Form 1.
_strings.@@cc4a76384af5: Additional Child and Dependent Care Tax Credit — You must have claimed the federal child and dependent care tax credit on your federal return, and you must have been a legal resident of Wisconsin for the entire year (on a joint return, qualifies if at least one spouse is a full-year Wisconsin resident).

_strings.@@ff2d1b106bbe: Renter's and Homeowner's School Property Tax Credit — Wisconsin filers who paid rent during 2023 for living quarters used as their primary residence, OR who paid property taxes during 2023 on their home. Available whether or not the homestead credit is claimed. Cannot be claimed if you or your spouse claim the veterans and surviving spouses property tax credit. Rent for property-tax-exempt housing (e.g., university dorms, nonprofit senior housing, certain public housing) does not qualify.

state_tax.work_common_tail: . Tax line: Form 1, Line 12 "Tax (see table on page 38)". Instructions p.16: "Use the amount on line 11 to find your tax in the Tax Table on pages 38-43... EXCEPTION If line 11 is $100,000 or more, use the Tax Computation Worksheet on page 44 to compute your tax." This op computes the state's rate-schedule tax line ONLY — county/city add-on taxes, state credits, and any amounts outside the rate schedule are NOT modeled. Pack notes: Base guidance: Supply 2023 Wisconsin Form 1, Line 11 ("Subtract line 10c from line 9. If line 10c is larger than line 9, fill in 0. This is taxable income"). Line 11 = Wisconsin income (Line 7) minus the sliding-scale standard deduction (Line 8, from the 2023 Standard Deduction Table, p.35) minus Line 10c exemptions ($700 x exemptions on Line 10a + $250 x age-65 checkboxes on Line 10b). Those deductions/exemptions must be computed on the form BEFORE supplying the base — this pack ships no standard deduction and no exemptions, so nothing is re-subtracted here. MID-YEAR RETROACTIVE RATE CUT: 2023 Wisconsin Act 19 (enacted July 2023, effective for taxable years beginning after December 31, 2022) reduced the first-bracket rate from 3.54% to 3.50% and the second-bracket rate from 4.65% to 4.40% (Wisconsin Tax Bulletin 222, July 2023, Item 6). Official 2023 documents printed BEFORE the act — notably the 2023 Form 1-ES instructions (D-101A, rev. 1-23) rate schedules — still show 3.54%/4.65% and are superseded; the filing-season 2023 Form 1 instructions ('New for 2023 — Tax Rates Reduced', Tax Table, and Tax Computation Worksheet) reflect the final rates shipped here. SOURCE ASSEMBLY: the 2023 Form 1 booklet prints no single four-bracket rate schedule. Brackets 1-2 (rates and dollar boundaries $13,810/$27,630 single-HOH, $18,420/$36,840 MFJ, $9,210/$18,420 MFS) are from Wisconsin Tax Bulletin 222 Item 6 (2023 amounts, sec. 71.06 as amended by Act 19); brackets 3-4 (5.3% up to $304,170/$405,550/$202,780, then 7.65%) are from the p.44 Tax Computation Worksheet. Cross-check: every worksheet subtraction constant equals the cumulative sum of the prior brackets at the final rates — Single/HOH $372.96 exact and $7,520.96 vs exact $7,520.955; MFJ $497.34 exact and $10,027.77 vs exact $10,027.765; MFS $248.67 and $5,014.00 exact — max divergence $0.005 (cent rounding), immaterial. TABLE MANDATE below $100,000 — Form 1 Line 12 requires the Tax Table (instructions pp.38-43) when Line 11 is under $100,000; the table computes tax at the midpoint of each $50/$100 income band, so bracket math may differ by a few dollars within table bands; the filed form must use the table. At $100,000 or more the mandated Tax Computation Worksheet IS exact bracket math (identical to this pack). STANDARD DEDUCTION NOT SHIPPED (income-dependent): Wisconsin's standard deduction is a sliding amount from the 2023 Standard Deduction Table (p.35) based on Line 7 income — maximums $12,760 single / $23,620 married filing jointly / $11,220 married filing separately / $16,480 head of household, phasing to $0 as income rises (e.g., $0 for single at $124,733+). Filers claimable as a dependent use the Standard Deduction Worksheet for Dependents (greater of $1,250 or earned income + $400, capped at the table amount); short-period filers and federal Form 4563 filers get $0. Compute it on Form 1 Line 8 — the supplied Line 11 base is already net of it. EXEMPTIONS NOT SHIPPED (already inside the Line 11 base): Wisconsin's exemptions ARE base reductions — $700 per exemption on Line 10a (taxpayer, spouse, and each dependent listed on federal Form 1040; $0 for a filer claimable as a dependent on another return) plus $250 on Line 10b for taxpayer and/or spouse 65 or older on December 31, 2023 (only if allowed the $700 on Line 10a) — but they are subtracted on the form in arriving at Line 11, so this pack ships none; do NOT re-subtract them from the supplied base. Head of household uses the SAME rate schedule as single (Tax Table column 'Single or Head of a household'; Tax Computation Worksheet Section A 'Single or Head of household'). Estates and trusts (fiduciaries) also use this schedule. QUALIFYING SURVIVING SPOUSE — engine mapping is WRONG for Wisconsin: Wisconsin has no QSS status; per the Form 1 instructions (p.13), 'If you file your federal return as a qualifying surviving spouse, you may file your Wisconsin return as head of household.' A federal QSS (spouse died 2021 or 2022) must therefore use the head_of_household brackets here, NOT married_filing_jointly. (A taxpayer whose spouse died during 2023 may still file 2023 as married filing jointly.) FULL-YEAR RESIDENT Form 1 ONLY: nonresidents and part-year residents file Form 1NPR and must PRORATE the tax brackets by the ratio of Wisconsin income to federal adjusted gross income — applying these brackets unprorated to a 1NPR filer is wrong. Credits taken after Line 12 are NOT modeled (they are subtracted from tax, not from income): itemized deduction credit (Line 13, Schedule 1 — claimed when certain federal itemized deductions exceed the Wisconsin standard deduction), renter's/homeowner's school property tax credit (Line 15), married couple credit (Line 17, Schedule 2), and other Form 1 credits.
